body:
`herdr-plugin-github-dash` is becoming **octoscope**, a standalone GitHub TUI that runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. The Herdr plugin integration is being retired.

## What changes

- The repository has been renamed to `kukv/octoscope` (old URLs redirect).
- The Herdr-specific launch path is gone: `herdr-plugin.toml`, `open.sh` / `run.sh`, the `HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON` context resolution and the `GITHUB_DASH_URL` link handler.
- It ships as a single binary named `octoscope` instead of a plugin.

## Why

The tool could only be started from inside a Herdr workspace, which turned out to be the wrong shape for something that is really just "look at my GitHub work". It also declared `platforms = ["linux", "macos"]` because its launch path was a pair of bash scripts — a limitation of this plugin, not of Herdr, which supports Windows plugins too.

Dropping the plugin wrapper makes it usable anywhere a terminal is, and opens the way to features the plugin shape made awkward: cross-repository views, diffs, reviews, checks, merge.

## Using it from Herdr

Nothing is lost. Bind a key to run `octoscope` via `keys.command` in your Herdr configuration and it opens exactly like before — it just runs as a normal command in a pane rather than as a plugin.

## Installing

See the [README](https://github.com/kukv/octoscope#install) — `mise`, a release archive, `go install`, or a source build.
title: Moving from a Herdr plugin to a standalone CLI (octoscope)
